title: The Fragmented Future

sourceEvidence.excerpt: The book begins with a tension rather than a forecast. AI may reduce the cost of expertise, translation, planning, legal interpretation, and administration, allowing smaller organizations and regions to handle complexity that once demanded a large bureaucracy. The same technology may also give states, continental blocs, and platforms extraordinary powers of surveillance, coordination, persuasion, and control. Both tendencies can occur together. “Fragmentation” therefore does not mean inevitable secession, ethnic partition, or romantic village life. The preferred hypothesis is constitutional and controlled: strong cities and regions nested inside federations that retain common rights, defense, redistribution, strategic infrastructure, and authority over large externalities. The book carefully separates current observations, historical analogies, uncertain scenarios, and normative judgment

sourceEvidence.locator: Political scale as a changing bargain
sourceEvidence.excerpt: History supplies mechanisms, not templates. City-states have supported participation, commerce, and institutional experimentation, but also oligarchy, exclusion, and war. Empires have built law, infrastructure, and long-distance order while extracting resources and suppressing difference. Federations distribute authority yet can entrench local injustice or suffer paralysis. The twentieth century rewarded national scale because mass armies, industrial supply chains, welfare systems, broadcast media, grids, and macroeconomic management favored standardization. AI may reverse only part of that settlement. A state can remain indispensable for security and redistribution without needing to control every school, permit, clinic, or development decision. Cheap cognition is not the end of scarcity. AI can multiply code, explanations, designs, lessons, and plans while leaving energy, compute, chips, land, water, trusted attention, care, security, institutional legitimacy, and ecological stability constrained. Some bottlenecks become more valuable precisely because synthetic output is abundant. This shifts political economy toward the infrastructure stack. Thousands of nominally independent firms or municipalities may still depend on one model provider, identity layer, cloud platform, or agent interface. Legal plurality can conceal technical centralisation. The book therefore distinguishes returns that compensate useful risk and coordination from rents earned by controlling unavoidable interfaces. sourceEvidence.locator: Elites, ambition, and meaning after work
sourceEvidence.excerpt: AI may weaken the informational monopoly once attached to professional expertise without eliminating hierarchy. Influence may migrate toward control of institutions, networks, physical assets, trusted brands, compute, and certification. The book’s deliberately provocative idea of “revocable nobility” treats privilege as an advance against a social function: authority and resources remain defensible only while the function is performed and open to challenge. Polycentrism can multiply arenas for useful ambition, but local elites may be especially entrenched through dense family, property, media, and contracting networks. A low-work future raises another difficulty. Employment supplies status, routine, social contact, and a sense of being needed as well as income. hook: AI could help a small city govern itself, while making it dependent on a distant platform.
readerPromise: Examine how AI can support both local capacity and concentrated dependency across political scales.
protectedRevelations: Final constitutional proposals, model outcomes and preferred institutional arrangements.
visualPlan: Smaller places, greater power: Show a local bus-service plan beside the distant provider needed to keep it working. Keep the local benefit and remote control in the same view without choosing an outcome.
Whose infrastructure?: A planner and resident discuss a nearby stop using shared technical assistance. Pull back to show neighboring places and regional infrastructure supporting the local plan.
The limits of independence: Follow the same river past two communities, keeping water and maintenance concrete. A local resident waits while a decision depends on a system outside the town.
Futures that divide: At the fallback office, place a local request beside a shared regional obligation. End on the ordinary route map and the book, with responsibility still under discussion.

visualActionChanges.direction: Open with the bus stop and planning room so political scale begins in daily life.
Keep local planner and remote provider visible together; omit the full outage sequence.
Use the river crossing a boundary as one concrete shared dependency.
End on the retained route and civic review, leaving the governance bargain unresolved.
